name: Philly Cheesesteak
desc: Thinly sliced ribeye with caramelized onions and melted provolone on garlic-butter toasted hoagie rolls.

source.title: Philly Cheesesteak
source.evidence: Same ingredients and amounts (1 lb ribeye, 1 large sweet onion, 8 slices mild provolone, 4 hoagie rolls, 2 tbsp butter with 1 pressed garlic clove, mayonnaise) and the same toast, caramelize, sear, melt order.

ingredients.raw: 1 lb ribeye steak, trimmed and very thinly sliced
1/2 tsp fine sea salt, or to taste
1/2 tsp black pepper, or to taste
4 hoagie rolls, sliced 3/4 of the way through

steps: Slice the hoagie rolls 3/4 of the way through with a serrated knife.

Stir the softened butter and pressed garlic together and spread it on the cut sides of the rolls. Toast cut side down on a large skillet or griddle over medium heat until golden brown, 2-3 min. Set aside.

Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan and cook the onion over medium heat until softened, about 5 min. Salt lightly and keep cooking, stirring now and then, until deep golden and caramelized, about 5 min more. Move to a bowl.
Raise the heat to high and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Spread the steak in an even layer and let it brown undisturbed, about 2 min.
Flip, season with the salt and pepper, and sauté until no pink remains, 1-2 min more. Stir the onions back in.
Divide the meat into 4 portions in the pan, lay 2 slices of provolone over each, and turn off the heat so the cheese melts without overcooking the meat.
Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on the toasted side of each roll. Set a roll open-side down over one portion, slide a spatula under the meat, and flip it into the bun. Repeat and serve warm.
tips: Freeze the ribeye for 30 to 45 min before slicing; it firms up enough to cut paper thin.
